question: Follow B1911 into its 2018 final reporting requirements and the 2020 submitted report. Register semiannual monitoring, annual certification and incident clocks without making the routine filing cure every reporting duty.
answer: Monitoring covers December 1–May 31 and June 1–November 30, due the last day of the following month unless a requirement is more frequent. All noncompliance must be identified and reports certified. Annual certification separately covers June 1–May 31, is due June 30 to District and EPA, and lists each requirement, status, continuity and method. Written incident notification is due within 10 calendar days of discovery; probable cause and corrective/preventive report within 30 calendar days of discovery. The submitted report expressly covers December 2019–May 2020; its existence does not establish incident-notice performance, regulatory receipt or all-program clearance.

question: Use the 2020 report to select Drivert Production S228 and contrast starch unloading/conveying S215/S216. Follow each into the final permit conditions and register inspection/correction/log requirements without assigning one frequency to every dust control.
answer: S228 is M-BH in the report and is listed under condition 17425: maintain the baghouse during source operation, equip pressure measurement within six months, retain the established range, and inspect pressure/visible particulate at least monthly. Out-of-range pressure or visible emissions triggers bag inspection, replacement of damaged/worn bags and reinspection. Monthly District-approved logs include date/time, inspector role, pressure comparison, visible check, conditional bag condition and corrective action, retained onsite five years from record creation. S215/S216 are annual in the report and condition 17426 instead requires visible checks while operating in daylight, corrective action and next-operation recheck if emissions occur. Reported routine frequencies do not prove every triggered inspection or repair was completed.

question: Prepare a cross-program acquisition finding for facility-026 from its 2020 air monitoring statement and 2025 water SEP order. Can the air report establish satisfaction of the water settlement or a clean inherited-liability conclusion?
answer: No. The company’s air statement is limited to December 2019–May 2020. The later water settlement’s resolution is expressly conditioned on timely full payment and full SEP implementation; after satisfaction, completion and any audits the Executive Officer issues a Satisfaction of Order. Those water gates are distinct from reported air inspections and noncompliance. Request payment, implementation, audit and satisfaction evidence without declaring the obligations unpaid or unfulfilled solely because the packet lacks receipts. A parent acquisition or a historical air report does not supply a regulatory release or private indemnity.
answer_facts: full payment of the administrative civil liability
